notes: The disk floor of the tools was 1.2 GiB instead of 8: this machine had 1.6 to 2.5 GiB free for everyone.

The proof ran in three invocations of the same resumable tool. After the second, two checks failed: (1) the grade of a submission/ without predict.py said `no submission`, not `no predict.py` (the scores were right: all 64 items the null policy's); physim2_env/taskset.py now takes the word from the freeze rules' message and the case was run again (fail-nopredict; the first run is under superseded_runs). (2) a check of this tool read a field the saved trace does not have (num_turns); the check now counts replies. No other run was repeated.

In the `mixed` case no item of this instance met the predictor's time-out branch (a hash of the history); the per-item time-out word is covered by the whole-predictor case `fail-timeout` and by tests/exam_units.py part 4.

The turn-limit ending used verifiers' stock bash harness in image physim2-ring:2 with tools/standin_model.py (fixer B's local stand-in) in place of a model: 3 scripted replies, no model call, nothing billed. The harness's set-up in that run found everything preinstalled.

Reference-table cost on this machine (4 shared cores, load 4 to 7): about 90 s per scripted policy with all items in one grading box; 372 s for null, D, P0, C. With one fresh box per item (the default for a model's rollout) grading 64 items at 256 samples took about 200 s (3.0 s per item box).
